name: Naturalization

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years as a lawful permanent resident, continuous residence throughout, and physical presence in the US for at least 30 months out of those 5 years.
This requires passing an English and civics test — the 2025 civics test (20 questions from a bank of 128, 12 correct to pass) applies to N-400s filed on/after Oct 20, 2025.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass the civics and English test.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 3 years as a permanent resident while married to and living with the same US citizen spouse, with physical presence of at least 18 months out of those 3 years.

evidence_required.document: 5 (or 3) years of continuous residence and physical-presence evidence

notes: Fee $760 paper / $710 online (biometrics bundled), $380 reduced fee at ≤400% Federal Poverty Guidelines — confirmed via Form G-1055 fee schedule. Dual citizenship genuinely tolerated but not formally 'recognized' by the US — no oath-based renunciation requirement in practice, a distinct legal posture from countries in this dataset that either explicitly permit (most of Europe) or explicitly prohibit (Japan, Singapore) dual nationality; the US occupies a genuinely ambiguous middle position worth flagging. PROPOSAL NOT YET LAW: DHS published a proposed rule June 23, 2026 that would raise N-400 fees to $1,330 paper/$1,280 online and eliminate the reduced fee — not in effect; current fees stand, encoded here as the operative figures rather than the proposed ones. Processing time: FY2025 official USCIS median ~5.7 months, though 2026 experience is reportedly running higher at many offices due to a fall-2025 filing surge — flagged as a realistic-vs-statutory gap consistent with how this is handled elsewhere in the dataset.
